doublage.contexte: Une discussion tendue entre un présentateur sceptique, un étudiant en colère et une envoyée officielle (probablement un représentant des autorités ou de l'administration) sur les manifestations lycéennes. L'étudiant explique ses revendications et rejette les accusations de dégradations, tandis que l'envoyée tente de modérer le ton. La scène se déroule dans un bureau administratif, reflétant le déséquilibre entre les attentes des jeunes et les réponses institutionnelles.

_anglais: But if you
ask for better conditions, why are you smashing things and burning down schools?
Dude, it’s crazy not to get it. We’re not smashing or burning anything—we’re just protesting, that’s it.
No, it’s not *just* that, excuse me, check the news.
The damage? Not us.
Then who?
I dunno, some idiots coming to stir the pot—they’re *not* part of the movement.
Yeah, but that’s *your* take.
Look, we just want people to hear us—that’s all.
We’re not here to trash places or break stuff.
So, what’s your
actual
demand here?
More teachers, more staff. I haven’t had physics class in three weeks.
Smaller classes, better learning conditions, fixing up these buildings.
You didn’t have to smash them to get that.
I *told* you...
Oh, okay, my bad—*not* you.
Also... less school pressure, lighter schedules. And scrap the ‘Parcoursup’ system.
Back in our day, we had all that and we still complained, so...
Not.
Wait, hold on—just ‘cause *you* took it doesn’t mean we gotta.
Seriously, have you seen the future they’re selling us?
Ugh...
Even with degrees, jobs are a nightmare these days.
And that’s *just* the start.
Come on, come on.
No, it’s *not* fine. We just want to study properly and pick our own future.
We don’t wanna be the screwed-over generation ‘cause of your meddling.
I kinda get it... sure...
Thanks, I guess. And *please*, don’t mix up the protesters with the troublemakers.
There’s already enough
confusion in this country.
I’ll watch it, promise. You’re sweet.
Alright, you can go.
Seriously, scram. And honestly? I think you’re right to do this.
Thanks, sir. Now piss off.
